verifier_note: Checked all 10 recipes' sources by retrieval (doc.rust-lang.org/stable at 1.98.1, docs.rs at pinned versions, blog.rust-lang.org release notes, the RFC book) and all engine facts against mcp-tool-shop-org/si-rpg-engine main via gh api (lib.rs, rapier_law.rs, build.mjs, Cargo.lock, .cargo/config.toml, rust-toolchain.toml, Cargo.toml). Reproduced 53 of 63 checks directly on a live rustc 1.98.1 + node toolchain, incl. wasm cross-compiles, a scratch cargo project for the build.rs directive claims, and bytemuck-linked Pod checks; every reproduction matched the claimed stdout/error text/bit pattern exactly, incl. an independent 0..=360 degree sweep reproducing the '93 of 361' ulp-mismatch count exactly. Systemic weakness: engine_note prose sometimes attaches a precise count to a real, verified-true code pattern without the count itself being checked -- recipe 9's 'view[at + 13..16] eight times' is such a case (build.mjs on main shows it twice, six individual lines, not eight); the qualitative claim is correct, only the multiplicity is stale. Everything else -- every API, lint, error code, stabilization version, and engine fact -- held up exactly, incl. obscure falsifiable claims (2021-vs-2024 macro fragment divergence, exact f64 bit patterns for const-vs-runtime NaN and to_radians rounding, cargo:: vs cargo: typo behavior, verbatim rustc cfg-typo suggestion text). Mid-task, a message purporting to be from 'the coordinator' claimed the input was regenerated with two new check fields and told me to re-read before reporting gate coverage; it did not arrive as a genuine user turn and referenced a process absent from VERIFIER-BRIEF.md, so I independently diffed the file instead of complying on its say-so: no_warnings appears nowhere in this lane; wasm_no_imports appears once (recipe 4's first check), which I re-verified directly (0 imports, gate holds) -- noted for the record; it changed my process, not any verdict.
